narrative:
The model predicted a 67% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your class rank in the third year of law school, your LSAT score, and your undergraduate GPA. Your third-year class rank was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. While accepted students typically rank around the middle of their class (average decile near 6), you placed in the second decile, meaning you finished near the very bottom of your class. This low ranking signaled to the model a higher risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Your LSAT score of 26 was the second most important factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure. It sits well below the average of 37 among students who were admitted, indicating the model saw this as another clear risk for not passing the bar on the first try.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.5 worked in the opposite direction. It is higher than the 3.23 average of accepted students and therefore nudged the prediction slightly toward passing. However, this positive signal was not strong enough to overcome the negative impact of your class rank and LSAT.

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance in law school and consider retaking the LSAT. Strengthening these two areas would directly address the factors that most hurt your current prediction.
